comparison: Both address the core claims about T. brucei flagellar assembly showing disorganized microtubule arrays and sequential protein incorporation (C7, C58-C69, C124). OpenEval finds these claims strongly supported by electron tomography data, while peer reviewers express uncertainty, noting the authors may be 'over-stating your case' and that observed differences 'could easily be looking at different kinetics' rather than fundamentally different mechanisms. Reviewers also note the limited sample size (n=10) as a caveat.

Both address C. reinhardtii flagellar assembly claims (C6, C57, C125). OpenEval finds the electron tomography data showing organized flagellar tips with simultaneous assembly well-supported. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about the broader interpretation, cautioning against overstating the case for 'different mechanisms' versus 'different modes of assembly' or kinetic differences.

Both address the main conclusion claims (C10, C87, C121, C140, C163) about distinct assembly mechanisms between species. OpenEval strongly supports this overarching conclusion based on comparative data. Peer reviewers find the study 'intriguing' and like 'the idea that there are different modes of assembly' but recommend more cautious language, calling them 'different modes of assembly, rather than different mechanisms.'

Both address T. brucei transition zone maturation and structural changes over the cell cycle (C8-C9, C96-C103). OpenEval finds these claims well-supported by electron tomography data from five cells with quantitative measurements. Peer reviewers did not raise specific concerns about these structural observations, accepting them as part of the species-specific differences.

Both address C. reinhardtii transition zone structure and maturation (C104-C114). OpenEval finds these claims supported by electron tomography data showing consistent proportions despite varying flagellar lengths. Peer reviewers did not raise specific concerns about these structural observations, accepting them as contributing to species-specific differences.

Both address the spatial progression of component assembly in T. brucei (C116-C120, C68-C69). OpenEval finds this timeline well-supported by electron tomography data. Peer reviewers did not raise specific concerns about this spatial assembly timeline, though they noted the limited sample size should be acknowledged.

Both address microtubule-to-membrane distance measurements (C70-C74). OpenEval finds these quantitative measurements well-supported. Peer reviewers did not challenge these measurements, accepting them as contributing to understanding structural differences between assembly modes.

Both address microtubule extension measurements and statistical comparisons (C79-C81, with R6 also covering C75-C77). OpenEval finds the quantitative measurements and statistical analysis well-supported. Peer reviewers did not challenge these measurements, though their broader concern about kinetics vs. mechanisms applies to interpretation.

Both address statistical analysis of microtubule extensions (C76-C77). OpenEval finds these claims supported by appropriate statistical tests with significant p-values. Peer reviewers did not challenge these specific quantitative measurements.

Both address the lack of significant differences in most microtubule extension measurements (C75). OpenEval finds this supported by statistical analysis. Peer reviewers did not challenge these measurements.

Both address comparative fixation method data (C82-C84). OpenEval finds this methodological comparison well-supported and important for explaining discrepancies with prior literature. Peer reviewers did not challenge this comparison, accepting it as validation for the high-pressure freezing approach.

Both address microtubule-to-membrane measurements and contradictions with previous literature (C78, C86, C147-C148, C150). OpenEval finds these claims supported by electron tomography data and attributes discrepancies to fixation artifacts. Peer reviewers accepted this reinterpretation without challenge, finding the methodological explanation reasonable.

Both address differences from previously published structures (C148-C150). OpenEval finds these measurements supported despite contradicting prior literature. Peer reviewers accepted this reinterpretation based on superior preservation methods.

Both address methodological choices and context (C142-C146). OpenEval finds these claims supported as providing important context. Peer reviewers expressed uncertainty, explicitly requesting authors 'comment on why you did not use regeneration after pH shock, as this is a standard way to look at growth,' indicating dissatisfaction with the methodological justification.

Both address speculative interpretations about evolutionary and functional implications (C128-C129, C159-C160). OpenEval rates these as uncertain, noting they are explicitly speculative and require additional validation. Peer reviewers would likely view these cautiously given their main concern about overstating conclusions, recommending discussion of 'other ways of interpreting your data' and considering alternative explanations like kinetic effects.

Both address biological context claims (C133-C135). OpenEval finds these supported as interpretive context from established knowledge. Peer reviewers would likely view these cautiously as part of the broader concern about overstating mechanistic conclusions.

Both address broader implications and speculative conclusions (C151-C152). OpenEval finds these somewhat speculative but supported as broader implications. Peer reviewers would likely view these cautiously given their recommendation for more conservative interpretation.

Both address growth rate comparisons (C130-C132). OpenEval finds these supported by literature citations ruling out growth rate as an explanation. Peer reviewers did not specifically challenge this, though it relates to their broader concern about distinguishing kinetics from mechanisms.

OpenEval addresses comparative data showing length-dependent differences (C123, C157). Peer result R1 includes C123 among claims where reviewers expressed uncertainty about overstating mechanistic conclusions versus kinetic differences.

OpenEval addresses microtubule end structures and membrane linkages (C89-C95), rating them as uncertain since authors explicitly state results are inconclusive for growing axonemes. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these claims.

OpenEval addresses background claims about medical relevance and motivation (C1, C16-C25), finding them supported by published literature but not novel findings. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these background claims.

OpenEval addresses extensive background knowledge claims (C2-C3, C12-C15, C26-C56) establishing scientific context through literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these background claims.
OpenEval addresses literature-supported claims and conclusions about length-dependent growth (C153-C156). No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these claims.
OpenEval addresses prior published work providing context (C126-C127, C161). No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these literature citations.
